items.title: Badge leaders crossed on MESHES at 1680x1050, because the layout score counted box overlaps and not crossings

must_fix.evidence: tests/headless.rs::no_two_leaders_cross was red from 2026-09-03; measured comfort score 1 (1 box overlap, 0 crossings) vs compact score 0 (0 overlaps, 3 crossing pairs)

items.evidence: tests/the_layout_score_counts_crossings.rs (2 tests, both fail on the unfixed code)

items.title: Twelve refusals were filed in Status::note, where the next receipt erases them

must_fix.evidence: A note is one dim row, erased by the next receipt and by a tab switch (Status::clear_note). A refusal there is a refusal the author never sees.

items.evidence: tests/every_refusal_is_in_a_problem.rs (2 tests; the first fails on the unfixed code with every site named)

items.title: The file watcher took ResMut<Project> and ResMut<OpenMap> every frame, and Bevy's conflict resolution deferred the badge layout past the frame

must_fix.evidence: The headless suite went from 189 pass / 0 fail to 2-4 failures whose set changed every run. Bisection: watcher disabled -> 189/0 twice; watcher as one system -> 2-4 fail, varying; watcher split into a tick and an act -> 189/0 twice.

items.evidence: crates/bevy_emerge_mapper/src/watch.rs (tick_watch and adopt_changes) and the headless suite

items.title: An agent can drive the editor through typed operations, over MCP, with the file changing under it

must_fix.evidence: Before: the editor's verbs were key handlers, so an agent could only synthesise keystrokes, and a data file edited on disk was invisible until a restart.

items.title: An operation per editor verb, with the UI and the agent both dispatching it

must_fix.evidence: The registry has one operation (map_set_settings) and 128 actions are on the unmigrated allowlist. The brief asks for one workflow first, with the allowlist shrinking.

items.title: The kit's library and policy are re-read by a full project reload, which is slow and loses the open map

must_fix.evidence: watch.rs::adopt re-opens the whole project for a library change, because only Project::open knows how to merge every bound kit. A per-kit re-read would be better.

items.title: The operation log has a single-writer assumption, so two agents would claim the same sequence number

must_fix.evidence: ops.rs::next_seq counts the lines in the log, and the MCP server and the editor are separate processes that could both append. An advisory file lock would fix it.

items.title: Enclosure wish and weight are hard-coded in the editor, so an author who wants more enclosed rooms edits Rust

must_fix.evidence: editor.rs ENCLOSURE_WISH = 0.25 and ENCLOSURE_WEIGHT = 200 are not in rules.ron, so they are not authored and cannot be tuned without a rebuild.

items.title: probe reports Ready for any non-loopback host without connecting, so a LAN endpoint that is down is reported ready

must_fix.evidence: probe() answered Reach::Ready for any host not spelled localhost/127./::1, so a LAN endpoint on a closed port was reported ready without a connect. The LAN bind is the documented portable setup; no config makes the preflight run there.

items.title: No crate in this workspace is published to crates.io, so the first publication is undecided

must_fix.evidence: cargo info for all seven crates says 'could not find ... in registry'. There is no published baseline, so no release can be made and no pre-publish gate has a version to check against.

items.evidence: cargo info bevy_emerge_core@0.1.0 (and the other six)

items.title: A map edited on disk reaches the editor's memory but not the screen: the placed pieces are spawned once, at open

must_fix.evidence: Wrong result on screen: the file says the piece moved, the editor's map agrees, the viewport does not (tests/a_map_edited_on_disk_reaches_the_screen.rs failed: 'piece on SCREEN is at Vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)'). Common: editing the map file is the hot-reload path. Workaround: restart the editor.

items.title: The chooser's new-map dialog writes name, bounds, origin and note directly, outside the registry

must_fix.evidence: chooser.rs:5907-5910 (write_settings) and chooser.rs:662 (write_bash) write the map's settings without dispatching map_set_settings. They are a different subject -- a new map with no open map -- and the honest claim is that one operation has two front ends, not that every verb does.

items.title: Undo is declared in the registry and performed by no tool

must_fix.evidence: ops.rs declares Undo::Inverse and Undo::Snapshot, the tool list names the strategy, and no tool performs an undo. The tool descriptions now say so rather than promising one.

items.last_failure: 2026-10-21: stopped on repeated failure (Non-negotiable 5). Tried to route emerge_undo through ops::dispatch by lending the editor's undo to ops::Ctx as a callback. Attempt 1: Box<dyn FnOnce + '_> needs a lifetime on Ctx, which every Ctx user would carry. Attempt 2: a 'static callback cannot hold the system's Commands/Res<AssetServer>/Query (E0521 'lifetime may not live long enough'). Hypothesis for next iteration: the flag-and-system shape E-007's fix uses -- the registry's undo operation queues a request (resource), an Update system in keys::Phase::Act pops EditorState::undo through the existing editor::undo body and records the log entry; the BRP command returns the queued operation id and the MCP tool polls emerge_state for the result, as emerge_capture_sequence already does. WIP patch (not committed): target/loop/2026-10-21-f9a9ac6/undo-wip.patch.
